<root_cause>
  <trajectory_summary>
  The agent inspected the three CSVs and extracted handbook text via pypdf (Turns 1–3). It identified the key handbook rules: preheat 100–150 °C, ramp < 2 °C/s, wetting time 30–60 s above liquidus, peak > liquidus + 20 °C (Turn 3 output). It examined MES columns, thermocouple structure (6 TCs per run at various locations), and defect summary rows (Turns 4–8). It then wrote /app/solve.py (Turn 10) implementing: Q1 max preheat ramp per run within 100–150 °C band, choosing the MAX ramp across TCs (worst-case for hardware stress); Q2 TAL via linear interpolation across the liquidus threshold, using MIN TAL across TCs (coldest sensor); Q3 peak temperature per run using MIN peak across TCs against liquidus+20; Q4 min conveyor speed derived as (board_length_cm/60 s)*60 to bound dwell to ≤60 s; Q5 best run per board_family ranked by fp_yield_pct then boards_per_min. Ran the script (Turn 11) producing all five JSON files; verified R0018 preheat ramp manually (2.08 °C/s, TC5) matched the output (Turn 13). Final message summarizes handbook constants and results.
  </trajectory_summary>
  <what_worked>
    <item>Turn 3: Successfully installed pypdf and extracted handbook text, surfacing the preheat 100–150 °C region, "less than 2°C/second" ramp limit, "30 to 60 seconds" wetting time, and "must be exceeded by approximately 20°C" peak margin.</item>
    <item>Turn 11: Script executed cleanly and produced all 5 JSONs (q01–q05) with correct schema (ramp_rate_limit_c_per_s=2.0, min_peak_by_run keyed by run_id, etc.).</item>
    <item>Turn 13: Manual verification for R0018 recomputed max preheat ramp = 2.084 °C/s on TC5, matching the JSON entry {"tc_id":"TC5","max_preheat_ramp_c_per_s":2.08}.</item>
    <item>Turn 10/11: Q3 correctly treats missing TC data as failing (script logic present); required_min_peak computed per-run from the run's actual solder_liquidus_c (e.g., 199, 203, 237 for the three paste liquidus values).</item>
    <item>Turn 10: Q2 TAL uses proper linear interpolation across the liquidus crossings rather than naive sample counting.</item>
  </what_worked>
  <issues>
    <issue>
      <where>Turn 10 / Q1 tc selection</where>
      <evidence>The script chose the MAX-ramp thermocouple across all 6 TCs (locations include largest_mass, smallest_mass, board_edge, center_BGA, connector_shield, near_heatsink).</evidence>
      <cause>The task says "select the most representative thermocouple value based on the handbook details." The handbook emphasizes that the largest-mass component is the critical thermal case (biggest mass is slowest to heat) — a common reflow-profiling convention is to use the largest-mass TC (which for ramp would actually give the lowest ramp, not the max). The agent's "worst-case = max across TCs" heuristic is plausible but is not directly justified from the handbook text; the intended answer may require TC1/largest_mass specifically.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>Turn 10 / Q2 & Q3 tc selection</where>
      <evidence>For TAL and peak the script picks the MIN across TCs ("coldest sensor").</evidence>
      <cause>Same interpretation risk: the handbook-representative TC is typically the largest-mass one (coldest). Coincidentally MIN often equals largest_mass, but the choice is heuristic rather than an explicit handbook rule, so the tc_id and even status classification for some runs may not match the grader's expected canonical TC.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>Turn 10 / Q4 minimum-speed formula</where>
      <evidence>required_min_speed_cm_min = (board_length_cm / 60) * 60, i.e., min speed = board_length_cm per minute; result: all 60 runs meet, non-meeting list empty.</evidence>
      <cause>The handbook's "board geometry, thermal dwell requirements, and allowable conveyor speed" likely requires a more specific derivation involving oven heated length and required time above liquidus / total profile time, not simply board_length/TAL_max. The formula chosen bounds dwell of a point on the board, but conveyor-speed feasibility in reflow ovens is usually governed by (heated-length)/(profile_time) with an upper limit as well. The trivially-passing outcome for all 60 runs is suspicious and suggests the derivation is off.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>Turn 10 / Q5 ranking criteria</where>
      <evidence>Ranking uses only fp_yield_pct then boards_per_min; runner-ups include runs like R0018 (Q1 violator) still listed for Wearable.</evidence>
      <cause>"Best run per board_family based on quality and efficiency" may require excluding runs that fail Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 compliance before ranking, or a combined score. The agent's implementation does not filter for compliance, which could differ from the expected best-run selection.</cause>
    </issue>
  </issues>
  <outcome_assessment value="uncertain">Handbook constants and computation mechanics are correct and verified, but the choices for "most representative TC" (Q1–Q3), the conveyor-speed feasibility formula (Q4), and the best-run criteria without compliance filtering (Q5) are interpretive and may not match the grader's expected canonical answers.</outcome_assessment>
</root_cause>
